title: A puzzle file, puzzles/<series>-<number>.json
description: An absent key means empty: no value is ever null, "", [] or {}; a clue the paper printed blank is {"missing": true}. A flag is written only when true. Checked on every write (tools/fetch_puzzle.py write_puzzle_file) and over the corpus in CI (tools/puzzle_schema.py).

number.description: The paper's puzzle number. Book puzzles carry volume * 1000 + position in the book.

name.description: The title as the paper gives it.

setter.description: The byline as printed. Absent when the paper names no setter, which Times, Telegraph and Metro puzzles never do.

date.description: The calendar day the paper printed it, YYYY-MM-DD (ISO 8601), in the paper's own timezone. A book puzzle holds `year` instead; a puzzle holds exactly one of the two.

year.description: The year a book puzzle's book was published, the most its imprint page prints (tools/data/books.json `published`). Only a book puzzle holds it, in place of `date`.

preamble.description: The paper's note above the clues: a themed puzzle's instructions, or an erratum.

annotatedBy.description: Who wrote the hints, in the order the runs happened: exact model ids, or tools/provenance.py ANNOTATORS. Present exactly when an entry has an annotation.

acquiredBy.description: tools/provenance.py ACQUIRED_BY: the command that wrote the file first.

annotator.description: tools/provenance.py ANNOTATORS; a model is named by its exact id instead.

position.description: The first cell, 0-based from the top left.

length.description: Cells in this light (a linked answer's other lights are separate entries).

solution.description: The answer, A-Z. Absent when the puzzle has no answers yet.

solutionConfidence.description: The letters are a model's likely fill, not the paper's.

group.description: On the leader of a linked answer only: the answer's entry ids in order, this entry first; an answer that repeats a light names it again. The other lights carry no group and no annotation; a light the clue says continues two answers is in both leaders' groups.

clue.description: The clue as the paper printed it. Every entry has one, with at least one key: a clue the paper printed blank is {"missing": true}.

text.description: The clue exactly as printed, enumeration included, e.g. "Moscow politician revolting in style (7)". The enumeration is not split out: about 9,500 clues print none or print a cross-reference ("See 5"), and printed ones vary ("(1'5)", "(6 and 5)", "(3/5)"); `separators` holds the word breaks in structured form. Absent only when the paper printed nothing at all, not even an enumeration (then `missing` is true). Offsets into it (`italics`, annotation `definitions[].at`) count Unicode code points.

separators.description: The marks the enumeration prints inside this light's answer, in answer order: (5,4) is [{"at": 5, "mark": ","}]. `at` counts this entry's own answer letters before the mark (1 to `length`), not clue characters; on a linked answer each light carries the marks inside it, and a mark at `length` falls between this light and the next light of its group. Absent when the answer is one word.

mark.description: As printed: "," is a word break and "-" a hyphen; rarely "'", ".", "/", ":", ";" or "and".

italics.description: Spans of `text` printed in italics, in order: text[at : at+length], counted in code points.

missing.description: The paper printed no words for this clue (`text`, if present, is only its enumeration). Kept, never filled in: a blank can be the setter's joke (cryptic-30098 12-across).

missingNote.description: A person's note on why the blank clue still gives its answer. Only with `missing`.

annotation.description: Our teaching annotation of one clue, on the leader alone for a linked answer. `blocks` are the wordplay as the app shows it, `assembly` is the same answer restated for a machine to check, and `explanation` is the prose the last hint rung prints. Keys marked required-by-ratchet are carried by every annotation written since each was added; older ones are counted per puzzle in tools/annotation_backlog.json under the key's dotted path (explanation.surface, indicators.note) and drained by the nightly backfill (tools/validate_annotations.py, the ratchet).

type.description: Every mechanism the wordplay uses, in the order applied.

answer.description: The solution in display form, spaced and hyphenated where the enumeration divides it; for a linked answer, the whole answer.

definitions.description: The clue words that define the answer, in clue order: one, or two for a double definition. `at` is the offset of `text` in the entry's `clue`, in Unicode code points, so clue[at:at+len(text)] == text. Where the text occurs more than once, `at` is the occurrence that (1) stands as whole words, (2) lies before the trailing enumeration, (3) does not overlap another definition, and (4) touches the clue's start or end, since a definition sits at one end of a cryptic clue; a text those rules leave ambiguous has its `at` given by hand (tools/definitions.py).

at.description: Offset of text in the clue, in Unicode code points.

note.description: Why the setter may define the answer this way, where the definition disagrees with the answer in number or part of speech.

definedByPreamble.description: The preamble, not the clue, defines this answer; replaces definitions.

indicators.description: One object per indicator phrase: the clue words, the clue type they signal, and why.

for.description: The one of this annotation's own types these words signal. Required by ratchet: absent only where tools/annotation_backlog.json grandfathers it, an allowance per puzzle that may only shrink (indicators.for).

note.description: Why these words signal that operation in this clue. Required by ratchet: absent only where tools/annotation_backlog.json grandfathers it, an allowance per puzzle that may only shrink (indicators.note).

linkWords.description: Clue words that join the definition to the wordplay and give no letters. Absent when the clue has none.

blocks.description: The wordplay, one block per clue fragment, in the order the answer reads (before a container, reversal or rotation is applied).

assembly.description: The answer rebuilt from the wordplay in forms a program can verify letter for letter, independent of `blocks`: blocks follow the clue's fragments and what the app shows, and often cut the answer differently. Every key is optional and absent when the clue has no such step; the whole object is absent when the clue has none (a hidden word, homophone, or double or cryptic definition has nothing to rebuild). tools/validate_annotations.py checks each key.

pieces.description: The answer in the chunks the wordplay builds, in answer order, joining to the answer's letters (LI, MITE, D for LID around MITE). Given for a charade, container or deletion; absent where an anagram is the whole assembly.

anagrams.description: Each anagram in the wordplay: its fodder and the letters it becomes, `fodder` a rearrangement of `gives`. When the whole answer is an anagram, one item's `gives` is the answer's letters (A–Z, no spaces); the others are anagrams inside the wordplay.

fodder.description: Every letter before shuffling, added ones included, as written (spaces allowed).

gives.description: The letters the fodder is shuffled into; the answer's letters when the whole answer is the anagram.

reversals.description: Each reversal in the wordplay: `to` is `from` read backwards.

to.description: The same letters back to front.

explanation.description: The prose a solver reads on the last hint rung, after the blocks: what the clue seems to say, how the trick works, and why the answer means the definition. Each is plain text, one or two sentences.

surface.description: One sentence, 25 words max, of the picture the clue pretends to paint. Required by ratchet on every clue of four or more words that is not a pure double or cryptic definition (absent only where tools/annotation_backlog.json grandfathers it under explanation.surface, an allowance per puzzle that may only shrink); on the others, absent when the clue paints no picture apart from its mechanism.

walkthrough.description: One or two sentences on what the blocks cannot show: why the surface misleads, a convention the solver may not know, why a definition is fair.

definitionFit.description: One sentence on why the answer means the definition. Required by ratchet: absent only where tools/annotation_backlog.json grandfathers it, an allowance per puzzle that may only shrink (explanation.definitionFit).

features.description: Required by ratchet: absent only where tools/annotation_backlog.json grandfathers it, an allowance per puzzle that may only shrink (features).

block.description: One piece of the wordplay: the clue words, and the letters they give. No gives means the words give no letters (an indicator or link).

select.description: Which letters the block keeps: a word, or n for the nth letter.

reversed.description: The block's letters go in back to front: `gives` is the letters before reversal ("charge" gives FEE, which the answer holds as EEF).

anagramOf.description: Anagram fodder: `gives` is the clue words' letters before they are shuffled.

features.description: Facts about the clue for analysis against solvers' favourites, never shown to a solver.

answerInScene.description: Does the solution belong in the picture the surface paints?

aptDefinition.description: Is the definition fresh or witty rather than a dictionary synonym?

joke.description: pun: the humour is in a word's second sense or sound; absurd: the surface is silly on purpose. Absent when there is no joke.

misdirectedWord.description: The one clue word, as printed, whose surface sense is furthest from its job. Absent when nothing misleads.

source.description: Where the puzzle came from. See tools/provenance.py.

url.description: The page the puzzle was printed on: the address to cite, not necessarily the one read (see retrievedFrom). Absent only on an authored puzzle.

acquiredOn.description: The day this repo first had the puzzle.

feedId.description: Metro only: the puzzle's id in the PuzzleMe feed it was read from.

solutions.description: Whose answers are in the grid. `blog`, `url`, `model`, `date`, `check` and `officialKey` back an origin that is not the publisher's: a writeup carries blog, url, date and check; a model solve carries model, date and check; any other origin carries none of them (tools/provenance.py check).

previousOrigin.description: The origin these answers replaced, when it differs: "model" for a grid we solved before the publisher printed its key.

url.description: The write-up the answers were taken from.

model.description: The model that solved the grid.

date.description: The write-up's date, or the day the model solved it.

check.description: What was verified against the grid.

officialKey.description: "never" when no official key will ever exist (tools/series.py).

blogFacts.description: Not part of a puzzle file: one puzzle's row of tools/data/blog_facts/<series>.json, which maps puzzle id to this. What one blog write-up marks about the puzzle's clues, read by parser rules only (tools/blog_facts.py, tools/letter_facts.py); each clue's facts use the annotation's own keys and shapes. Checked in CI by tools/puzzle_schema.py.

name.description: The blog's name as a reader knows it.

entries.description: Entry id -> blogFact, for the clues the write-up marks something about.

blogFact.description: One clue's facts from a blog write-up: a partial annotation, with the same key names and shapes.

definitions.description: As annotation.definitions, without notes: the span the blogger underlined, or both halves of a double definition, in clue order, `at` placed by tools/definitions.py. A text those rules cannot place is left out.

typeCore.description: `type` is a lower bound: the clue is that, and perhaps a cut or a letter selection besides.

indicators.description: The words the write-up marks as indicators, and the type each signals where it says.

inferred.description: The fields tools/letter_facts.py read off the answer's letters rather than off the write-up.

blogBlock.description: One piece of a blog's wordplay, as an annotation block: the clue words and the letters they give.

soundsLike.description: A homophone's or spoonerism's piece: the word the clue words say, which `gives` sounds like.

anagramOf.description: Anagram fodder: `gives` is the clue words' letters before they are shuffled.

inferred.description: A piece tools/letter_facts.py split the answer into; the write-up did not name it.
